name: Active Directory
description: Microsoft's directory service for Windows domain networks, managing authentication, authorization, and centralized administration of users, computers, and resources.

name: Active Directory Federation Services
description: Microsoft service that enables single sign-on and identity federation across organizational boundaries using claims-based authentication protocols.

name: Auth0
description: Identity-as-a-service platform providing authentication, authorization, and user management features for web and mobile applications via APIs and SDKs.

name: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM)
description: Amazon Web Services feature for managing users, groups, roles, and permissions to control access to AWS resources securely.

name: Azure Active Directory
description: Microsoft's cloud-based identity and access management service, enabling single sign-on and secure access to applications for organizations.

name: Azure Active Directory B2C
description: Microsoft's customer identity access management service that lets businesses add sign-up, sign-in, and identity management to consumer-facing apps.

name: Checkmarx
description: Static application security testing tool that scans source code to identify security vulnerabilities during development.

name: Cisco Duo
description: Access security platform providing multi-factor authentication and device trust verification to protect user logins and applications.

name: Dependabot
description: GitHub-integrated tool that automatically checks project dependencies for known vulnerabilities and opens pull requests to update them.

name: Ghidra
description: Open-source software reverse engineering framework developed by the NSA, used to disassemble and decompile binaries for security research and malware analysis.

name: Google OAuth
description: Google's implementation of the OAuth 2.0 protocol, allowing applications to obtain limited access to user accounts and Google APIs.

name: JSON Web Token (JWT)
description: Compact, URL-safe token format used to securely transmit claims between parties, commonly for authentication and authorization in web applications.

name: Metasploit
description: Penetration testing framework used by security professionals to develop, test, and execute exploit code against target systems.

name: OAuth
description: Open standard protocol that allows applications to obtain limited access to user accounts on another service without exposing passwords.

name: OAuth 2.0
description: Authorization framework version that enables third-party applications to obtain limited access to a user's resources via access tokens.

name: Okta
description: Cloud-based identity management service offering single sign-on, multi-factor authentication, and user directory services for organizations and applications.

name: OpenID Connect
description: Identity layer built on top of OAuth 2.0 that allows applications to verify user identity and obtain basic profile information.

name: OpenSSL
description: Open-source toolkit that implements the SSL/TLS protocols and provides cryptographic functions used for secure communications.

name: PKCE
description: Extension to OAuth 2.0 that prevents authorization code interception attacks, commonly used in mobile and single-page applications.

name: Prisma Cloud
description: Cloud security platform that provides posture management, workload protection, and compliance monitoring across multi-cloud environments.

name: SAML
description: XML-based open standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between identity providers and service providers, often used for single sign-on.

name: Snyk
description: Developer security platform that scans code, dependencies, containers, and infrastructure-as-code for vulnerabilities, integrating into development workflows.

name: SonarQube
description: Open-source platform for continuous inspection of code quality, detecting bugs, vulnerabilities, and code smells across many programming languages.

name: ThreatLocker
description: Endpoint security platform that uses application allowlisting, ringfencing, and access control to prevent unauthorized software execution and limit attack surfaces.

name: Veracode
description: Application security platform offering static, dynamic, and software composition analysis to find and remediate vulnerabilities in code.
